system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915, a syllabary built for Swedish (i/j, u/v/w, a/å/ä, o/ö not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms (1287 storviziren = Grand Vizir, 1713 grefwen = comte, 1516 ottporten = Porte, 1511 hof = Cour, 1448 fred = paix, 1360 tractat = traité). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d', 1251' = dé, 1500' = à).
system.notes: Seed values read by eye only in the first build; the key was then rebuilt from the glossed despatch (235 confirmed values) and extended by 24 values from Lit. A's gloss. Key: key.tsv of this folder (as on origin/main 54c4ecc65), applied frozen and unchanged; key_1741.tsv adds 24 values read from the Lit. A gloss and corrects two single values of it (1504 vo, 1840 au). Lit. B (vol. I/9/29, catalogue 2242) is read with key_1741.tsv unchanged; it is Latin. 31 groups that are in neither key take a value guessed from sense there (46 places, each group with one value throughout; listed in NOTES.md); 1461 (fi) stands for ni twice and 1471 (ga) for Latin ia twice.

prior_solution.where: The contemporary Swedish decipherment written over the groups on images 322-327. No edition or modern decipherment found (web searches, 10 Nov 2026). Castellane's own letters of 1740-47 are in the French diplomatic archives (Nantes), not checked.

texts.summary: Höpken and Carlson report to the King how the Porte's dragoman brought the signed defensive alliance treaty and asked to delay its exchange and keep it secret, how they argued for a prompt exchange, and how the exemplars were exchanged on 14/25 January 1740 after a present to Ragib Efendi. They credit the King's firmness over the Russian frontier, note the French ambassador's late help, and ask for a provisional instruction and full powers.

texts.label: Lit. A, image 147: memorandum on the last Russo-Ottoman treaty
texts.summary: The more one examines the last peace treaty between the Porte and the Muscovites, the more one finds conditions onerous and unbearable for the Sultan, manifest contradictions, and attempts to deceive the Porte, which the Muscovites treated as an inferior prince on whom they meant to impose laws; this is to be shown article by article, beginning with article 2 on the frontiers (breaks off).
texts.note: Read through the contemporary gloss, checked group by group against the frozen hopken1740 key (79% exact on the gloss, held out). Against the frozen key: 84 of 122 words verbatim, 3 with a marked repair, 35 resting on values read from this gloss. The cipher differs from the gloss in four places, followed in the reading. The page ends mid-sentence; the continuation was not looked for.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: the whole page reads; 84 of 122 words come from the frozen hopken1740 key and the rest from values the contemporary gloss gives over the same groups. 23 groups of this page (92 over the three pages) were spot-checked on the image with no disagreement.

texts.label: Castellane to Höpken and Carlson (cipher copy), image 49 L01-L16
texts.summary: After a general divan at the Porte, the Porte's dragoman invited Castellane on behalf of the Grand Vizier to a kind of congress next Sunday at which Monsieur de Romanzof (probably Rumyantsev, the Russian ambassador) is to be present; he asks the Swedes for their reflections before the sieur de Laria goes to the Porte's dragoman next morning at eight.
texts.note: 94 cipher words: 79 verbatim from the key (84.0%), 2 with a marked repair, 13 resting on context-guessed values, no holes. Every sentence is coherent French; the guessed values are mostly single syllables fixed by the sense, three of them also by recurrence in the reply. In 'le sieur de Laria aille' the cipher writes one a for two (marked {+a}). Checker clean share 0.444, just under 0.45, because it counts each guessed word as a hole.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: all four sentences hold; 13 words rest on syllable values guessed from context and are marked, and none leaves a gap in the sense. Checker share 0.444.

texts.label: Höpken and Carlson to Castellane (cipher copy), image 49 L17 to the foot of image 50 left page
texts.summary: The Swedes thank Castellane for his generous conduct toward the interests of their court, announce a visit next evening to set out their thoughts on Sweden's present interests with regard to Russia and Russia's differences with the Porte, and begin to say that in Sweden's critical situation with Russia any accommodation between the Porte and Russia is ... (breaks off at the foot of the page).
texts.note: 123 cipher words to the foot of the left page of image 50: 109 verbatim (88.6%), 3 repaired, 10 guessed, 1 hole (1515). One clear sentence. Checker clean share 0.615. The text continues on images 50 (right page), 51 and 52, not transcribed.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: the four sentences hold to the break at the foot of the page; one group is unread and 10 words rest on marked context values.

texts.label: Lit. B (duplicate copy), Latin letter signed Ibrahim Effendi, vol. I/9/29 images 81-82
texts.summary: Latin letter signed Ibrahim Effendi to an Excellency: he has explained again and again the boundaries to be marked and the law and custom for dividing the islands; the 'legatus Germaniae' (probably the Imperial envoy) was astonished and did not know what to answer; he expects him to stop disputing about the islands and to accept everything today or tomorrow; he was given leave to call on the addressee but was kept at the Porte all day and asks to be excused.
texts.note: 169 cipher words: 113 verbatim from the signs (66.9%), 13 with a marked change of a key value (74.6% together), 40 resting on values guessed from sense, 3 holes ([1463], [1909], and one two-group word in B09). Two digits were corrected after the blind review (C10 g4 1024, B15 g16 1495?). Dan's checker: clean share 0.348 (8 of 23 sentences); its Latin word list lacks several ordinary words of this letter, see NOTES.md.

reading_review.note: Read as Latin sentences against the translation: real Latin chancery prose that follows through from the greeting to the address, with 3 true holes; many words rest on marked guessed values. About 115 groups were copied from the image blind; the 2 disagreements were corrected before sending.

texts.label: Lit. A: extract of the translation of the Khan of Crimea's letter to the King of Sweden, May 1742
texts.summary: The Khan, after reaching the Porte, tells the King of Sweden that the delay in executing the Swedish-Ottoman defensive alliance comes only from the Porte's need to fortify its frontier with Persia; aid promised to friends is conditional, so aid to Sweden is difficult, but the Ottoman Empire values Sweden's friendship and will give all the aid it can in the present circumstances.
texts.note: 256 cipher words: 205 verbatim from the frozen key (80.1%), 23 repaired, 28 from the gloss only, 0 holes; 22 of the verbatim words rest on a pass-3 digit re-read. Held-out: 487 of the 602 glossed groups match the gloss (81%; 88% of the 554 in the key; shuffled maximum 103 over 300 shuffles). Checker clean share 0.900 (reading, 27 of 30 sentences), 0.912 (translation). A contemporary decipherment checked against the key; the bare runs of the volume remain open.
